subject.title: [Bug]: startup legacy-state migration never converges when .migrated archive already exists; gateway permanently refuses to start

question: Which convergence rule should OpenClaw use for already-imported legacy residue that cannot be archived to the default `.migrated` path or cannot resolve a session owner?
rationale: The fix affects persisted-state cleanup and the gateway fail-closed startup boundary, so maintainers should choose the rule before an automated repair removes, re-archives, or downgrades these warnings.

options.title: Retire verified imported residue
options.body: After proving the canonical SQLite/plugin state contains the imported data, delete the legacy source or move it to a non-colliding archive while keeping real conflicts as warnings or blockers.

options.title: Downgrade successful-import residue
options.body: Keep the files in place but classify already-imported residue as a non-blocking notice during startup, leaving doctor to provide cleanup guidance.

options.title: Keep fail-closed cleanup
options.body: Preserve the current warning-as-blocker behavior and document manual cleanup for operators who hit archive collisions or ownerless sidecars.

recommendation.title: Retire verified imported residue
recommendation.body: After proving the canonical SQLite/plugin state contains the imported data, delete the legacy source or move it to a non-colliding archive while keeping real conflicts as warnings or blockers.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant behavior sits in the database-first state migration and Codex binding migration work they authored and merged.
